docs.title: swishbot
docs.text: A Claude Code plugin that distributes data stack skills, agents, and project scaffolding for Swish BI. Install once — get 8 skills, 3 agents, hooks, MCP servers, and slash commands.

docs.title: What is swishbot?
docs.text:
swishbot distributes self-contained skills, agents, hooks, MCP servers, and slash commands for data engineering and analytics work.

Skills are opinionated methodology guides that Claude reads to understand how to execute specific tasks. Each skill encodes how to think about the problem, not platform-specific implementation details. Claude already knows the platforms (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, etc.) — skills teach it how you think.

Agents are persona definitions that compose multiple skills into a focused role (e.g., data-engineer, platform-engineer). They give Claude a specific identity for a type of work.

Hooks enforce rules automatically — SQL validation, credential checks, and more — without any manual setup.

MCP servers connect Claude to external tools like dbt, Dagster, dlt, and Power BI.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Claude Codeskills.sh 
# Add the swishbot marketplace
/plugin marketplace add swishbi/swishbot

# Install the plugin
/plugin install swishbot@swishbot

npx skills add swishbi/swishbot

Follow the interactive prompts to install.

Everything is now available:

  • 8 skills auto-loaded
  • 3 agents in /agents
  • Hooks active
  • MCP servers configured
# Scaffold a new project
/swishbot:scaffold my-client-project

# Set up project config
/swishbot:init-project
/swishbot:init-memory

No pip install. No Python dependency. Pure Claude Code native.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. Install the plugin — via skills.sh or native Claude Code commands
  2. Skills, agents, hooks, and MCP servers auto-load — no per-skill install step
  3. Use slash commands — /swishbot:scaffold, /swishbot:init-project, /swishbot:init-memory, /swishbot:migrate
  4. Work with Claude — Claude reads the skills and applies the methodology to your project

Skills are platform-agnostic at the methodology level. They encode consistent, best-practices guidance that Claude applies to whatever stack you're working with.

docs.title: Zero-touch team onboarding
docs.text:
Add this to your project's .claude/settings.json (checked into version control):

{
  "extraKnownMarketplaces": {
    "swishbot": {
      "source": {
        "source": "github",
        "repo": "swishbi/swishbot",
        "ref": "stable"
      }
    }
  },
  "enabledPlugins": {
    "swishbot@swishbot": true
  }
}

New team members clone the repo, open with Claude Code, and are prompted to accept the plugin. No manual steps.

docs.title: Agents Catalog
docs.text:
Agents are persona definitions that compose multiple skills into a focused role. When you use an agent, Claude takes on that identity and applies the relevant skills together.

All agents auto-load when the swishbot plugin is installed — no per-agent install step. Invoke an agent by asking Claude to "act as the data-engineer agent" or by selecting one from /agents.

docs.text:

docs.title: /swishbot:scaffold
docs.text:
Scaffold a complete analytics project with ingestion, transformation, orchestration, and CI/CD.

/swishbot:scaffold my-client
Argument Description name Project name (kebab-case)

docs.title: What gets created
docs.text:
my-client/
  ingestion/              # dlt pipelines
  transformation/         # dbt project (models, seeds, macros, tests)
  orchestration/          # Dagster orchestration with dlt/dbt/Power BI components
  tests/                  # Project tests
  .claude/                # CLAUDE.md, SECURITY.md
  .devcontainer/          # VS Code Dev Container for local development
  .github/workflows/      # Dagster Cloud deployment workflows (disabled by default)
  pyproject.toml          # Project config with all dependencies
  dagster_cloud.yaml      # Dagster Cloud location config

The project name is substituted throughout — pyproject.toml, dbt_project.yml, dagster_cloud.yaml, deployment workflows, and the Dev Container config all use the name you provide.

docs.title: Dev Container
docs.text:
The scaffolded project includes a .devcontainer/ directory for VS Code Dev Containers. Open the project in VS Code and select Reopen in Container to get a fully configured development environment with Python, uv, Dagster, dbt, and dlt ready to go.

Pre-installed VS Code extensions: Claude Code, Python, Pylance, Ruff, YAML, dbt Power User, Better Jinja, TMDL.

docs.title: Dagster Cloud deployments
docs.text:
The .github/workflows/ directory includes two GitHub Actions workflows for Dagster Cloud:

  • deploy.yml — Deploys to production on push to main
  • branch_deployments.yml — Creates branch deployments on pull requests

Both workflows are disabled by default. They will skip until you enable them:

  1. Set up your Dagster Cloud organization
  2. Add the following GitHub repository secrets: DAGSTER_CLOUD_API_TOKEN, ORGANIZATION_ID
  3. Add a GitHub repository variable: DAGSTER_CLOUD_ENABLED = true

The DAGSTER_CLOUD_URL in each workflow is set to http://<project-name>.dagster.plus — update this if your Dagster Cloud organization name differs from the project name.

docs.title: /swishbot:init-project
docs.text:
Create a starter CLAUDE.md and SECURITY.md in your project directory.

/swishbot:init-project

Both files are created together — CLAUDE.md defines project conventions and skill references, while SECURITY.md provides security guidelines for SQL safety, credential handling, and prompt injection defense.

docs.title: /swishbot:init-memory
docs.text:
Scaffold a project memory directory with templates for Claude to persist decisions across sessions.

/swishbot:init-memory

This creates a .claude/memory/ directory with template files:

  • MEMORY.md
  • conventions.md
  • modeling-decisions.md
  • source-catalog.md

docs.title: /swishbot:migrate
docs.text:
Migrate an existing dlt + dbt project into the swishbot structure with Dagster orchestration.

/swishbot:migrate ./my-existing-project
Argument Description dir Project directory to migrate (defaults to current directory)

docs.title: What happens
docs.text:
The command runs in 5 phases:

  1. Discovery — scans for dlt pipelines (@dlt.source, .dlt/), dbt projects (dbt_project.yml), existing Dagster config, and project files
  2. Restructure — moves dlt pipelines to ingestion/, dbt project to transformation/ (uses git mv in git repos)
  3. Dagster orchestration — copies orchestration templates and creates placeholder defs.yaml with TODOs for each detected pipeline
  4. Project config — merges pyproject.toml dependencies, .gitignore entries, .mcp.json servers; sets up .claude/ with CLAUDE.md, SECURITY.md, memory templates
  5. Summary — prints what moved where and a TODO checklist for manual follow-up

Key principles: confirms before moving files, merges config (never overwrites), uses git mv to preserve history, creates placeholder TODOs rather than broken configs.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text:
Hooks are Claude Code event handlers (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop) that enforce rules automatically. When the plugin is installed, all hooks are active — no manual setup required.

Current hooks:

Skill Event Matcher Script dba-security PreToolUse Bash validate-sql.sh iac-terraform PreToolUse Bash validate-terraform.sh

Hook scripts use ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} paths to locate scripts within the plugin directory.

docs.title: MCP servers
docs.text:
MCP servers are auto-configured via the plugin's .mcp.json. No manual setup needed. Available servers:

Server Description dbt dbt project introspection and MetricFlow queries dagster Dagster asset and job management dlt dlt pipeline and source inspection powerbi Power BI semantic model and report management

docs.title: Memory architecture
docs.text:
/swishbot:init-memory sets up shared project memory — a single .claude/memory/ directory that all agents contribute to and read from. This fills a gap that native Claude Code memory mechanisms don't cover:

Memory type Path Scope Managed by Per-agent memory .claude/agent-memory/<agent-name>/ Single agent Auto-managed by Claude Code (memory: project) Shared project memory .claude/memory/ All agents + main session Updated manually or via MEMORY.md conventions

Per-agent memory is declared with memory: project in each agent's frontmatter. Claude Code automatically creates .claude/agent-memory/<agent-name>/MEMORY.md and injects it into the agent's system prompt at startup — no configuration needed. Use this for agent-specific learnings.

Shared project memory is what /swishbot:init-memory creates. All agents read it at session start. Update these files manually or ask Claude to update them when cross-agent decisions are made (naming conventions, modeling choices, source quirks).

To also load shared memory in the main session (not inside an agent), add an @ import to your CLAUDE.md:

@.claude/memory/MEMORY.md

The project CLAUDE.md template (from /swishbot:init-project) includes a commented-out version of this import — uncomment it after running /swishbot:init-memory.

docs.title: Create a new skill
docs.text:
Create a new skill directory under plugins/swishbot/skills/:

mkdir plugins/swishbot/skills/my-new-skill

Add a SKILL.md file with YAML frontmatter and methodology content.

Tip

The skill-creator skill can help you create and iterate on new skills. Ask Claude to "create a new skill" and it will guide you through the process.

docs.title: Skill anatomy
docs.text:
Every skill has at minimum a SKILL.md with this structure:

---
name: skill-name
description: "When to use this skill and what it does."
---

# Skill Title

## Overview
What this skill does and the methodology behind it.

## Methodology
Your opinionated approach — the reasoning and patterns
that make Claude work the way you would.

## Patterns
Concrete patterns with examples. Show what good output looks like.

## Anti-Patterns
What to avoid — the mistakes you've seen that Claude
should steer away from.

*Copyright (c) 2026 Swish BI Limited. All rights reserved.*

docs.title: Frontmatter
docs.text:
The YAML frontmatter at the top is required:

  • name — the skill directory name (kebab-case)
  • description — a short description of when to use this skill. Keep it on one line (extracted via regex). Write it as an implicit trigger: include natural-language phrases users would say when they need this skill.

Optional frontmatter fields recognized by Claude Code:

  • argument-hint — hint text shown to users (e.g., "[source-name]")
  • hooks — Claude Code event handlers (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop) that enforce rules automatically. See Hooks below.
  • user-invocable, disable-model-invocation, allowed-tools, model, context, agent — additional Claude Code skill fields

docs.title: Optional additions
docs.text:
Skills can include extra directories:

  • references/ — examples, templates, lookup tables that the skill references
  • scripts/ — helper scripts the skill can invoke (often referenced by hooks)
  • workflows/ — step-by-step procedures for multi-step tasks, routed from the SKILL.md body
  • examples/ — example files and patterns

docs.title: Workflow routing
docs.text: Skills with multiple workflows use SKILL.md as a router that maps user intents to specific workflow files. Add a routing table in the markdown body (not frontmatter) that maps intents to workflow files in workflows/<workflow-name>.md. Each workflow is a focused, step-by-step procedure.

docs.title: Writing methodology
docs.text:
Skills encode how to think about problems, not platform-specific implementation details. Focus on:

  • What to do and why — Claude already knows the platforms
  • Patterns — concrete examples of good output
  • Anti-patterns — common mistakes to avoid (often the most valuable part)

The goal is to make Claude work the way you would, applying your experience and opinions consistently.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text:
Skills can define hooks in their frontmatter to enforce rules automatically. Hooks fire on Claude Code events like PreToolUse (before a tool runs) or PostToolUse (after). A hook can be a command (runs a script) or a prompt (asks Claude to verify something).

Example frontmatter with a hook:

---
name: my-skill
description: "Example skill with a pre-tool hook."
hooks:
  PreToolUse:
    - matcher: "Bash"
      hooks:
        - type: command
          command: "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/my-skill/scripts/validate.sh"
          timeout: 10
---

Place hook scripts in scripts/ inside the skill directory. Hook scripts must use ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} paths — this ensures they work correctly when installed as a plugin.

When the plugin is installed, hooks from all skills are merged into plugins/swishbot/hooks/hooks.json and auto-loaded. No manual hook configuration needed.

docs.title: Testing a skill
docs.text: During development, test your skill by running Claude Code against a real scenario in the plugin repo. Iterate on the SKILL.md until Claude produces correct output on the first shot.

docs.title: New skill checklist
docs.text:
When adding a new skill, complete every step:

  1. Create the skill directory in plugins/swishbot/skills/<skill-name>/
  2. Write SKILL.md with YAML frontmatter (name, description, optional argument-hint) and methodology content
    • description must be a single line (extracted via regex); include natural-language trigger phrases
    • End file with copyright footer: *Copyright (c) 2026 Swish BI Limited. All rights reserved.*
    • For skills with workflows: add a routing table in the markdown body that maps intents to workflow files
  3. Add optional subdirectories if needed: workflows/, examples/, scripts/
  4. Add cross-references to related skills in a ## Related Skills section
  5. Update related skills to cross-reference back to the new skill
  6. If the skill has hooks: add them to plugins/swishbot/hooks/hooks.json using ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} paths
  7. Update the status table in README.md — add the skill row and set status to :white_check_mark:
  8. Update the CATEGORIES dict in docs/hooks/skills_catalog.py — add the skill to the correct category
  9. Run uv run ruff check tests/ docs/ and uv run ruff format tests/ docs/
  10. Run uv run pytest -v — all tests must pass
  11. Bump version in plugins/swishbot/.claude-plugin/plugin.json

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Clone the repo:

    git clone https://github.com/swishbi/swishbot.git
cd swishbot

  2. Install in dev mode with test dependencies:

    uv sync --extra test

  3. Set up pre-commit hooks:

    uv run pre-commit install
uv run pre-commit install --hook-type pre-push

docs.title: Running checks
docs.text:
# Lint
uv run ruff check tests/ docs/

# Format
uv run ruff format tests/ docs/

# Tests
uv run pytest -v

If you installed the pre-commit hooks, lint and format run automatically on every commit, and tests run before every push. CI also runs all three on every PR.

docs.title: CI
docs.text:
CI runs on every push to main and on all pull requests. It tests against Python 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, and 3.13:

  1. ruff check — lint
  2. ruff format --check — format verification
  3. pytest -v — tests

docs.title: Commit checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] uv run ruff check tests/ docs/ and uv run ruff format tests/ docs/ pass
  • [ ] uv run pytest -v passes
  • [ ] Version bumped in plugins/swishbot/.claude-plugin/plugin.json if release-worthy
  • [ ] If skills changed: update status tables in README.md, and CATEGORIES in docs/hooks/skills_catalog.py
  • [ ] New skills have correct name and description in frontmatter
  • [ ] If hooks changed: update plugins/swishbot/hooks/hooks.json

docs.title: What you get
docs.text: Component Count Description Skills 10 dbt, dagster, dlt, dimensional-modeling, powerbi, cube, requirements-discovery, dba-security, iac-terraform, tech-docs Agents 3 data-engineer, business-analyst, platform-engineer Hooks Auto SQL validation, Terraform validation MCP servers 4 dbt, dagster, dlt, powerbi Slash commands 4 scaffold, init-project, init-memory, migrate

docs.title: Set up your project
docs.text:
Generate a starter CLAUDE.md and SECURITY.md in your project directory:

/swishbot:init-project

This creates files that:

  • Define project conventions
  • Describe your project structure and platform environment
  • Provide security guidelines for SQL safety, credential handling, and prompt injection defense

Edit CLAUDE.md to fill in your project details. Claude reads this file to understand your project context and apply the right skill guidance.

docs.title: Set up project memory
docs.text:
Scaffold a memory directory so Claude can persist modeling decisions, source metadata, and conventions across sessions:

/swishbot:init-memory

This creates .claude/memory/ with template files. There are two distinct memory systems at work:

  • Per-agent memory — Each agent (data-engineer, business-analyst, etc.) automatically manages its own .claude/agent-memory/<agent-name>/ directory via memory: project. No setup needed.
  • Shared project memory — /swishbot:init-memory creates .claude/memory/ for cross-agent decisions (naming conventions, modeling choices, source quirks) that all agents read and contribute to.

After running init-memory, uncomment the @ import in your CLAUDE.md to also load shared memory into the main Claude session:

@.claude/memory/MEMORY.md

See Commands & Setup for the full memory architecture.

docs.text: Open Claude Code in your project. Skills auto-load from the plugin — Claude will automatically apply the methodology when working on relevant tasks. Try asking Claude to build a dbt model or write a dlt pipeline.

docs.title: Skills Catalog
docs.text:
Skills are self-contained methodology guides that Claude reads to execute data engineering and analytics work. Each skill encodes opinionated, platform-agnostic guidance for a specific layer of the data stack.

All skills auto-load when the swishbot plugin is installed — no per-skill install step. Claude invokes skills automatically based on the task at hand, or you can reference a skill by name (e.g., "use the dbt skill").

Some skills include hooks — Claude Code event handlers that automatically enforce rules when Claude writes or edits files. For example, dlt validates for hardcoded credentials and dba-security checks for SQL permission patterns. Hooks are active as soon as the plugin is installed.

docs.title: Discovery & Planning
docs.text: Skill Description requirements-discovery Act as a business analyst to guide stakeholders from idea to implementation-ready requirements. Use when a user asks to scope a report, run a discovery session, gather requirements for a dashboard, produce a developer specification, interview SMEs, extract business rules, document column-level logic, or map business logic to staging columns.

docs.title: Infrastructure
docs.text: Skill Description dba-security Apply DBA security best practices. Use when a user asks to set up warehouse roles, configure access controls, create database environments, set up dbt grants, implement row-level security, or audit permissions. Applies to Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Postgres, and DuckDB. iac-terraform Deploy analytics infrastructure as code with Terraform. Use when a user asks to provision Snowflake warehouses, BigQuery datasets, Databricks workspaces, GCS/S3 storage buckets, IAM roles, or Azure AI Foundry resources for data platform services.

docs.title: Ingestion
docs.text: Skill Description dlt Write and maintain dlt/Python data ingestion pipelines. Use when a user asks to ingest data from an API, database, or file into a warehouse, create a new EL pipeline, debug a failing pipeline, add a new endpoint to an existing pipeline, handle schema changes, change write dispositions or primary keys, retire a resource, or tune pipeline performance.

docs.title: Orchestration
docs.text: Skill Description dagster Orchestrate data pipelines with Dagster and Dagster+. Use when a user asks to set up a Dagster project, create assets, configure components, wire dlt or dbt into Dagster, define schedules, or debug orchestration issues.

docs.title: Transformation
docs.text: Skill Description dbt Build the dbt transformation layer. Use for any dbt work — staging sources, building intermediate models, creating marts, applying SQL conventions, setting up dbt MCP, debugging errors, or reviewing project structure. dimensional-modeling Apply dimensional modeling best practices. Use when a user asks to design a star schema, choose grain for a fact table, handle slowly changing dimensions, conform dimensions across sources, or structure a bus matrix.

docs.title: Analytics & Presentation
docs.text: Skill Description powerbi Apply Power BI best practices. Use when a user asks to build a report, design a Power BI semantic model, write DAX measures, set up deployment pipelines, configure workspaces, connect Excel to a dataset, parameterize M queries, or plan a Power BI rollout. cube Build and secure the Cube semantic layer on self-hosted Cube Core. Use when a user asks to model a dbt mart as a cube, define measures or dimensions, join a fact to its dimensions, create a view for Metabase or an AI agent, set up Cube's SQL API users, restrict who can query what, handle balances that must not sum over time, or check that Cube's numbers match the warehouse.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: Skill Description tech-docs Use when writing technical documentation for data platform work — setup guides, runbooks, data dictionaries, pipeline READMEs, architecture notes, troubleshooting guides, or multi-document reference suites.
